Be our expert-level Priority Habitat and Species (PHS) Habitat Connectivity Biologist! In this role, your work will make lasting contributions to the department’s goals to conserve and protect a resilient network of native fish and wildlife habitat in Washington state.

As the technical lead for habitat connectivity mapping and planning, you’ll apply your expertise in wildlife habitat connectivity science to identify priority areas for connectivity conservation and translate that science into practical tools, guidance, and land-use planning strategies. You’ll work across urban and rural landscapes to help protect and restore wildlife movement and build climate-resilient habitat networks.


What to Expect:
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Habitat Connectivity Biologist will,

Incorporate spatial data identifying priority habitat connectivity locations in Washington state into the Priority Habitat and Species (PHS) framework:
Translate new and existing habitat connectivity data into a format appropriate to PHS applications.
Develop technical documentation of methods used to create spatial data.
Develop user guides for application of habitat connectivity data.
Develop management recommendations for protecting wildlife habitat connectivity priorities within land use and transportation planning context.

Identify spatial data identifying priority habitat connectivity locations in Washington state:
Identify appropriate existing spatial data to locate areas important to landscape connectivity and barriers to wildlife movement.
Evaluate and make recommendations about existing spatial data relative to the best available science standard defined in Washington state code (WAC 365-195-915).

Provide technical assistance for the development and application of wildlife habitat connectivity data in the context of land use planning and land management:
Provide technical assistance on the applications of PHS habitat connectivity data to internal and external users in the context of local land use planning, transportation planning, growth management, and shoreline management.

Represent the agency in a technical capacity in efforts to create new wildlife habitat connectivity data products and strategies:
Participate in research activities including data collection, evaluation, and analysis, to identify priority locations for connectivity protection, restoration, and enhancement.
Participate in working groups developing wildlife habitat connectivity data products, priorities, and implementation strategies.
 

Working Conditions:

Work Setting, including hazards: Primarily an office setting, with partial remote work options available. A minimum of 20% of work time is expected to be in person.

Schedule: Typically Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., or an equivalent schedule. Flexible schedule options may be available after successful completion of the probationary/trial service period.

Travel Requirements: Approximately 5–10% travel is expected for meetings and field visits to review connectivity project proposals and implementation. May include required travel to locations throughout the state for which carpooling or public transit options are not available.

Tools and Equipment: Standard desktop or laptop computer workstation and specialized software, such as ArGIS.

Customer Interactions: Regularly interact with Division and Section-level management, staff from other WDFW programs, Regional Habitat Program staff, city and county planning staff and directors, consultants, other state agency staff, and natural resource and conservation non-governmental organization partners. And occasionally interact with local elected officials and tribal natural resources staff.


Qualifications:

Closely related qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-by-year basis.

Required Qualifications: 

Option 1:
Four (4) years as a Fish & Wildlife Biologist 3.

Option 2: 
A bachelor’s degree or higher in biology, conservation biology, landscape ecology, fisheries, wildlife management, natural resource science or management, environmental science, or related field.
       AND
Five (5) years of professional experience in fish management or research, wildlife management or research, or habitat management or research. 

In addition, the following competencies are also required: 
Demonstrated success in fostering a collegial, collaborative, and productive work environment with colleagues who are not co-located.
Excellent time management skills.
Strategic thinker who also demonstrates close attention to detail.
Successful demonstration of strong critical thinking skills applied to solving complex natural resources problems.
Ability to adapt to changing needs or ability to be flexible as needs of the position change. 
Ability to communicate effectively verbally and in writing. 
Ability to take interest in and understand others' perspectives, easily recognize when others have important information, perspectives, or ideas, demonstrate appropriate assertiveness, and be committed to the service of the public, mission, and team.

Please Note: 
Master’s degree in the applicable science may substitute for one (1) year of the required experience. 
A Ph.D. in the applicable science may substitute for two (2) years of the required experience.

Certifications/Licenses: Valid driver’s license.


Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess one or more of the following:

Experience:
Demonstrated relevant experience working in wildlife habitat connectivity conservation. 
Relevant experience may include field research, spatial modeling or analysis, remote sensing, and/or natural resources management within a university, local government, environmental or conservation organization, consulting firm, or state or federal natural resources agency.
Proficiency with GIS and execute basic spatial analytical tasks in a GIS framework including knowledge of ArcGIS desktop and ArcGIS Online software.

Competencies: 
Expert knowledge of landscape ecology, conservation biology, conservation planning, or similar discipline.
Expert knowledge of wildlife habitat connectivity science and modeling approaches.
Demonstrated ability to understand and explain spatial data characteristics and applications.
Demonstrated ability to conduct spatial analysis and manage large databases.
Ability to synthesize complex spatial information and develop analyses in written and visual form.
Ability to perform complex geoprocessing and manipulate large datasets using scripts.
Knowledge of scripting (such as Python or SQL) to automate spatial analysis tasks.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex scientific concepts to policy makers, planners, or other non-scientists.
Knowledge of principles, methods, and objectives of urban and natural resources planning.

Description
Study animal behavior, provide daily care, learn applied conservation skills and support herd management of wildlife in large habitats that keep wildlife wild.  

Gain hands-on experience and launch your career in animal husbandry, learning conservation skills side-by-side with expert wildlife specialists at White Oak!  

Nestled along the St. Mary's River in mixed wetland and forest habitats, White Oak is a working conservation facility with over 17,000 acres of land focused on species recovery, education, and habitat restoration. White Oak has an impressive track record of rehabilitation and reintroduction programs, including work with Florida grasshopper sparrows, Florida panthers, and Mississippi sandhill cranes. White Oak is a proud member of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA). 

Interns provide 40 hours of service per week and must be available for the duration of the internship. Interns receive on-site housing and a monthly stipend. We are proud to have a high graduation rate of interns moving on to full-time roles as zookeepers or wildlife biologists with conservation organizations through this internship program. 

 

Career-Ready Skills & Learning Opportunities  

Interns are provided with a variety of projects designed to give the technical skills and knowledge that makes them well qualified candidates for a variety of roles across conservation facilities such as:  

Animal husbandry skills including cleaning, feeding, diet prep, diet stocking and organization  
Knowledge of different animal behaviors, including identifying vocalizations, body language/postures, reproductive behaviors, and social dynamics  
Safe animal capture, hand restraint, and transportation  
Habitat maintenance including landscaping and fabrication  
Basic research skills in observation training, sample collection, note taking and reporting  
Medicating and tracking health outcomes of animals in collaboration with our veterinary team  
Observation of advanced veterinary care practices, procedures and necropsy  
Cross training on days off, or as opportunities arise 
 

Application Instructions 

Interested individuals must complete an online application. All Wildlife Husbandry Internships have a commitment length of 6 months. Incomplete applications, or applications submitted outside of a recruitment window, will not be considered. 

Interns select which teams they wish to intern with as part of the application process. Available internship placements are detailed below. 

Please note that the application window is open for approximately one month, followed by an additional 3–4 weeks for teams to review applications and select candidates for interviews and intern positions. 

Wildlife Husbandry Intern Application: https://www.volgistics.com/appform/1362526948  

 

Rhino & Ungulate Team 

White Oak's Rhino & Ungulate Teams care for a rainbow of species including white, black, and greater one-horned rhinos, giraffe, okapi, exotic equids and a variety of antelope and gazelle species. Interns learn animal care hands-on from day one, working with some of the largest populations of these imperiled species. 

Specialized skills in herd management, manual restraint, neonate care, animal introductions and animal body language are available to high-achieving interns in the program. 

 

Conservation and Recovery Department (CaRD) 

White Oak's CaRD team provides interns with amazing experiences working with species recovery programs with a focus on avian species, including cranes, sparrows and cassowary species. Interns help with catch-ups, breeding programs, reintroduction work, and more.  

Specialized skills in conservation, reintroduction programs, artificial incubation, research, controlled burn procedures and insect management are available to high-achieving interns in the program. 

 

Carnivore Team 

White Oak's Carnivore Team cares for carnivore species such as Florida panthers and tigers, and manages one of the largest and most successful cheetah breeding programs in North America. Interns learn a variety of skills in carnivore care and behaviors.  

Specialized skills in animal identification, carnivore diet prep, breeding behaviors, shifting techniques, real-time problem solving and behavioral conditioning are available to high-achieving interns in the program. 

 

Elephant Team 

White Oak's elephant team proudly cares for one of the largest populations of Asian elephants in the Western hemisphere. Interns should have a clear or growing interest in elephant husbandry and operant conditioning.  

Specialized skills in animal management, observing operant conditioning training sessions and bathing elephants, learning social dynamics and novel elephant behavior are available to high-achieving interns in the program.

Have previous experience working with animals, domestic or exotic (internships and/or volunteer work counts!) 
Experienced and comfortable working outside in high heat and humidity 
Strong attention to detail and data management skills 
High drive to learn, take on challenges, and stay motivated 
Be flexible to changing environments, priorities, or animal care needs 
Able to lift 50 lbs. repetitively, and remain standing, walking or crouched over for long periods of time 
Able to work 40 hours per week for the duration of the internship 

Interns receive housing and a monthly stipend of $2,400 (before taxes)

Learn more about being a member of Team WDFW! 


This position plays a key role in shaping how WDFW-managed lands and recreation opportunities are planned, managed, and enjoyed. The Planning and Recreation Section (P&RS) Manager serves as the principal planning and recreation consultant to the Wildlife Program Lands Division Manager (LDM), providing leadership and expertise on complex planning and recreation issues.

In this role, you’ll coordinate the development and implementation of environmental resource plans, programs, policies, and regulations related to the management of more than 1,000,000 acres of WDFW-managed lands and more than 480 water access sites that support recreational and commercial fishing and boating opportunities. 

You’ll also provide leadership on outdoor recreation and visitor use management, travel management, and efforts to address recreation-related impacts while protecting natural and cultural resources. The P&RS Manager represents the agency’s planning and recreation interests both internally and in collaboration with other agencies, partners, stakeholders, and the public. 


What to Expect:
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Planning and Recreation Section (P&RS) Manager will, 

Lead and direct the Planning and Recreation Section: 
Manage the P&R Section and provide guidance on policy and planning to other technical staff within the Department.
Supervise, plan, assign, and review the work of P&R Section employees, adjust assignments and schedules to respond to fluctuating workloads or constraints to deliver complete projects.
Develop and implement strategic and operational planning for the P&R Section.
Ensure P&R Section work products conform with WDFW Strategic Plan, the agency’s Conservation Principles, the 10-year Recreation Strategy, and other relevant agency positions, commitments and guidance.

Direct Management Planning for Wildlife Areas (WLA) and Water Access Areas (WAA):
Direct and guide production of quality WLA and WAA Management Plans.
Provides oversight of multi-disciplinary teams to advance Departmental conservation and recreation goals and facilitate solutions for WLA and WAA specific challenges.

Manage Recreation on DFW-Managed Lands:
Lead development of recreation management policies, procedures, and rules for WDFW-managed Lands. 
Lead and support implementation of recreation and access policies, procedures, and rules.
Ensure clear communication of recreation and access opportunities and rules with the public.
Facilitate cross-agency collaboration on recreation issues with other state land managers.
Provide leadership and/or strategic planning to address emerging recreation management needs.
Lead efforts to support responsible recreation on WDFW-managed lands and water access areas.

Represent WDFW in Key Planning and Recreation Partnerships:
Lead WDFW efforts to remain a recognized partner and leader in balancing conservation with compatible recreation in Washington State. 
Develop and maintain partnerships to facilitate recreation planning and management with Tribes, other state and federal land managers, conservation and recreation groups, boards, commissions, and the legislature. 

Participate in Lands Division Leadership Team:
Participate in and share leadership of regular Lands Division Leadership Team and Lands All-Staff meetings.


Working Conditions:

Work Setting, including hazards: Office environment (95%) with occasional tours or site visits to WAA or WLA locations throughout the state (5%). Hazards may involve exposure to inclement weather, uneven or unstable terrain, slippery surfaces, vegetation, insects, wildlife, and other natural hazards. This position may involve working in or near water, including tasks that require navigating, negotiating, and performing duties related to water environments.
 
Schedule: Typically, Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM, with infrequent evening or weekend meetings, tours, or site visits.
 
Travel Requirements: Occasional travel for meetings, conferences, or for site visits, infrequent overnight travel may be authorized.
 
Tools and Equipment: Standard office equipment and software such as Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Adobe Acrobat, SmartSheet, Garmin GPS, and mobile phone applications.
 
Customer Interactions: Interact primarily with other professionals within and outside of the Department. This role requires participation in public forums including briefings for the Fish and Wildlife Commission and various Committees, Citizen Advisory Committees, Tribal Roundtable discussions, and various conferences and meetings in which public comments and interaction are solicited.
 

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:

Option 1 – All of the following (experience may be gained concurrently):
A Master's degree or higher with a major emphasis in one of the following: 
Land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning.
Landscape architecture.
Geography.
Land use or environmental law.
Public administration with an environmental emphasis.
A closely related field.
Five (5) years of professional experience in land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning, and/or program development.
One (1) year or more of leadership or supervisory experience, including conflict resolution, training and development, planning and assigning work, and evaluating performance.

Option 2 – All of the following (experience may be gained concurrently):
A Bachelor’s degree with a major emphasis in one of the following: 
Land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning.
Landscape architecture.
Geography.
Land use or environmental law.
Public administration with an environmental emphasis.
A closely related field.
Seven (7) years of professional experience in land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning, and/or program development.
One (1) year or more of leadership or supervisory experience, including conflict resolution, training and development, planning and assigning work, and evaluating performance.

Option 3 – All of the following (experience may be gained concurrently):
Eleven (11) years of professional experience in land use, urban, regional, environmental, or natural resource planning; landscape architecture; geography; land use or environmental law; public administration with an environmental emphasis; program development; or a closely related field.
One (1) year or more of leadership or supervisory experience, including conflict resolution, training and development, planning and assigning work, and evaluating performance.

Certifications/Licenses:
Valid driver’s license.
 

Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess one or more of the following:

Knowledge and Abilities:
Knowledge of planning principles, techniques, and current trends; environmental laws, policies and programs related to recreation, cultural resources, and natural resource development; government administrative structures; and challenges affecting planning and recreation programs.
Knowledge of recreation, cultural, and natural resources planning and objectives, as well as principles of staff supervision.

Leadership:
Ability to organize, coordinate, and lead programs, processes, and multidisciplinary teams; assign and monitor work; and guide others toward project goals and objectives.
Ability to interpret information, evaluate options, and recommend decisions or courses of action to management based on project goals and multidisciplinary team input.

Communication Skills:
Experience presenting information to groups, preparing written and verbal reports and recommendations, and analyzing and interpreting information to identify effective options and courses of action.

Facilitation and Organizational Skills:
Experience facilitating meetings and collaborative processes to make decisions, solve problems, develop plans, and resolve disputes.
Experience building collaborative relationships, identify areas of common interest, and gather, research, and organize information from diverse sources.

Planning Skills:
Experience developing and implementing strategic plans for WDFW-managed lands, including Wildlife Area plans, recreation management, outreach, and Discover Pass initiatives.
Experience evaluating proposed actions and timelines against organizational mission and values, integrating plans across programs and disciplines, and making informed decisions regarding the relevance, feasibility, and overall value of plans.
Experience developing instructional materials and guidance for implementing legislation, rules, policies, procedures, and program strategies.
